statement: Individual financial statements are generally prepared under IFRS in Europe.
explanation: Wrong. The EU IFRS Regulation only requires IFRS for the CONSOLIDATED statements of LISTED companies. Individual (separate) statements of legal entities are generally prepared under local GAAP (they serve tax and dividend purposes); some countries allow or require IFRS for them, France does not. That is why subsidiaries' statements must first be converted to IFRS before consolidation.

statement: A group is an economic entity composed of different legal entities.
explanation: Correct. Each legal entity (parent, subsidiaries) prepares its own individual statements; the consolidated statements present the group as ONE economic entity – as if parent and subsidiaries were a single company (e.g. IAG with British Airways, Iberia, Vueling).

statement: Company A owns 10% of entity E1. Based on this percentage of ownership, E1 is included in the scope of consolidation of A.
explanation: Wrong. With 10% of the voting rights A normally has neither control nor significant influence (presumed from 20%). The investment is a passive financial asset measured under IFRS 9 – E1 is not consolidated and not equity-accounted. (Only other facts, e.g. board representation, could create significant influence.)

statement: Company A has a controlling influence on entity E2. E2 is included in the scope of consolidation of A.
explanation: Correct. Control (IFRS 10) → E2 is a subsidiary and is fully consolidated: 100% of its assets, liabilities, income and expenses are included, with non-controlling interests shown separately if A owns less than 100%.

statement: Company A owns 0% of entity E3. It is absolutely impossible to include E3 in A's scope of consolidation.
explanation: Wrong. Consolidation is based on CONTROL, not ownership. A can control an entity without holding shares – e.g. a structured/special purpose entity governed by contracts where A has power over the relevant activities and is exposed to variable returns. Then E3 must be consolidated (IFRS 10).

statement: The only possibility to control another company is to own more than 50% of its voting rights.
explanation: Wrong. More than 50% creates a presumption of control, but control can also exist with less: shareholders' agreements, the right to appoint the majority of the board, double voting rights, potential voting rights, or a dispersed shareholding of the other investors. Conversely, >50% may not give control if another party has contractual power.

statement: Goodwill is always equal to the difference between the purchase price of the shares and the book value of these shares.
explanation: Wrong. First the purchase price allocation (PPA) assigns the difference to identifiable assets and liabilities at fair value (valuation differences, e.g. brand names, higher fair value of buildings). Goodwill = purchase price − FAIR VALUE of the identifiable net assets acquired (× % acquired). Only the remainder (synergies, workforce, market position…) is goodwill.

statement: Consolidated net income = net income of the parent + 100% of the (post-acquisition, adjusted) net income of the subsidiary, even when the parent owns less than 100%.
explanation: Correct. Under full consolidation 100% of the subsidiary's revenues and expenses are included because the parent controls them. The result is then split into a group share and a non-controlling interest share (e.g. 60% subsidiary with NI 20: group share 12, NCI 8).

statement: Non-controlling interests provide equity to a subsidiary. Therefore, they are included in consolidated equity.
explanation: Correct. Minority shareholders are owners of the subsidiary, not creditors – their share of the subsidiary's net assets is presented in consolidated EQUITY, separately from equity attributable to owners of the parent (IFRS 10.22).

statement: The equity method consists in measuring the investment in an associate at fair value (e.g. market value).
explanation: Wrong. Under the equity method (IAS 28) the investment is initially recognised at cost and then adjusted for the investor's share of the associate's post-acquisition changes in equity (mainly profit/loss, less dividends received). Market value is irrelevant; the investment appears as one line in the balance sheet and the share of profit as one line in the income statement.

statement: A negative goodwill (badwill) is recognised immediately as a gain in the income statement of the year of acquisition.
explanation: Correct. If the fair value of the identifiable net assets exceeds the purchase price (bargain purchase), IFRS 3 requires the acquirer to reassess the PPA and then recognise the remaining difference immediately as a gain in profit or loss.

statement: A positive goodwill is amortised over its useful life under IFRS.
explanation: Wrong. Goodwill has an indefinite useful life under IFRS: it is NOT amortised but tested for impairment at least annually (at the level of the CGU(s) to which it is allocated). Goodwill impairment losses can never be reversed.

statement: Companies over which the parent has significant influence are fully consolidated.
explanation: Wrong. Significant influence (presumed from 20% of voting rights) makes the company an ASSOCIATE, accounted for using the equity method (IAS 28) – one line in the balance sheet and in the income statement, no line-by-line integration, no NCI.

prompt: Match the type of relationship with the accounting method. Which pair is NOT correct?

options.text: Control (subsidiary) – full consolidation (IFRS 10, IFRS 3)
Significant influence (associate) – equity method (IAS 28)
Joint venture – equity method (IFRS 11/IAS 28)
Joint operation – proportionate recognition of its share of assets/liabilities
Passive investment below 20% – equity method

explanation: Passive investments are financial assets under IFRS 9 (fair value). Thresholds are indicative: 20% significant influence, >50% control.

prompt: Which of the following is NOT a step of full consolidation?

options.text: Purchase price allocation: fair value–book value differences and goodwill
Integration of 100% of the subsidiary's assets, liabilities, income and expenses
Elimination of intra-group transactions, in particular investment in subsidiary vs. subsidiary's equity
Identification of non-controlling interest
Measurement of the investment at market value

explanation: Before that: determine the scope of consolidation and prepare the individual statements (convert to IFRS, uniform accounting policies, currency conversion).

prompt: Calculate the goodwill paid by Palma at the acquisition.
explanation: Book value of Ibiza's equity = 400 + 1,000 + 200 = 1,600. Fair value of identifiable net assets = 1,600 + brand 600 = 2,200. Goodwill = 2,600 − 2,200 = 400 K€. (1,000 would ignore the brand name.)

prompt: What is the total of Palma's consolidated balance sheet at the acquisition date?
explanation: Land 700 + other NCA 2,800 + brand 600 + goodwill 400 + current assets 1,400 = 5,900. Equity = Palma's equity only (3,400) + liabilities 2,500 = 5,900. The investment (2,600) is eliminated against Ibiza's equity (1,600) + the valuation difference (600) + goodwill (400).

prompt: What is the goodwill in the PC/SA acquisition?
explanation: SA equity = 200 + 825 + 175 = 1,200. Fair value of net assets = 1,200 + brand 600 + building 400 = 2,200. Goodwill = 3,000 − 2,200 = 800. Expected synergies are NOT an identifiable asset – they are part of goodwill.

prompt: Which amount does NOT appear in PC's consolidated balance sheet at the acquisition date?

options.text: Brand name 600 and goodwill 800
Share capital 900 and retained earnings 1,210
Equity of 4,010 including SA's equity

explanation: PP&E = 4,600 + 870 + 400 fair value adjustment = 5,870; brand 600 and goodwill 800 are recognised. Consolidated equity at acquisition = parent's equity only (900 + 700 + 1,210 = 2,810); SA's pre-acquisition equity is eliminated, so there is no equity of 4,010. Synergies are part of goodwill, not a separate asset. Total = 10,660.

prompt: Which amount does NOT appear in the consolidated balance sheet of 31 December N2?

options.text: Goodwill 350
Brand name 200
Net income 260
Equipment 1,050 and liabilities 1,150
Capital 1,000

explanation: Goodwill = 900 − 300 − 250 = 350 (unchanged). Brand impaired by 50 → 200. Consolidated NI = 120 + 190 − 50 = 260. Capital = parent's capital only (700); SA's capital of 300 is eliminated. Total 2,110.

prompt: On 31 December N3 the brand name's value rises to 400 €. What is the accounting impact?

options.text: Reversal of the impairment of 50 – the brand goes back to 250 (gain in P/L)
The brand is revalued to 400 with a gain of 200
No impact – impairments are never reversed
Goodwill increases by 150

explanation: Impairment losses on assets other than goodwill must be reversed when the reason no longer exists, but only up to the carrying amount without impairment (here the original 250, as the brand is not amortised).

prompt: Which amount does NOT appear in the consolidated balance sheet at 31 December N (acquisition date)?

options.text: Non-controlling interest 60
Total assets 310
Equity attributable to the parent 100
Goodwill 0
Non-controlling interest 90

explanation: NCI = 40% × 150 = 60. Purchase price 90 = 60% × 150 → no goodwill. Assets = 140 + 170 = 310, liabilities 150, group equity 100.

prompt: What is the split of consolidated net income at 31 December N+1?

options.text: Group share 42, NCI 8
Group share 50, NCI 0
Group share 38, NCI 12
Group share 30, NCI 20

explanation: Consolidated NI = 30 + 100% × 20 = 50, of which NCI = 40% × 20 = 8 and group share = 30 + 12 = 42.

topic: Full consolidation vs. equity method error
prompt: Mamy owns 70% of Filia (borrowings €500,000) and has exclusive control, but consolidated Filia by the equity method. This mistake …

options.text: had no impact on the group's financial debt
reduced the group's financial debt by €350,000
reduced the group's financial debt by €500,000

explanation: Under full consolidation 100% of Filia's liabilities would be included (500,000), irrespective of the 70% ownership. The equity method shows only one investment line, so the full 500,000 of debt is missing (exam 2024).

prompt: F owns 70% of E1, acquired for 1,000. E1's equity was 800; a piece of land recorded at 100 had a fair value of 280. What goodwill is recognised (parent's share)?
explanation: Fair value of net assets = 800 + (280 − 100) = 980. Group share 70% × 980 = 686. Goodwill = 1,000 − 686 = 314.

prompt: M owns 80% of F, acquired for 600 when F's equity was 750 (share capital 500, reserves 250). At 31/12/N: M: share capital 800, reserves 1,500, NI 400; F: share capital 500, reserves 300, NI 100. What is consolidated equity attributable to the group?

options.text: Share capital 800, group reserves 1,540, group NI 480
Share capital 1,300, reserves 1,800, NI 500
Share capital 800, reserves 1,800, NI 500
Share capital 800, reserves 1,500, NI 400

explanation: Goodwill = 600 − 80% × 750 = 0. F's post-acquisition reserves = 300 − 250 = 50 → group share 40 → reserves 1,540. Group NI = 400 + 80% × 100 = 480. Only the parent's share capital appears.

prompt: Can a parent control another company while owning only 45% of its shares?

options.text: Yes – e.g. through a shareholders' agreement, the right to appoint the majority of board members or shares with double voting rights
No – control always requires more than 50% of the shares
Only if the parent also holds more than 50% of the company's debt
Yes, but the company is then accounted for with the equity method instead of full consolidation

explanation: Control (IFRS 10) = power over relevant activities + exposure to variable returns + ability to use power. Voting agreements, board appointment rights or double voting rights can give power below 50%.

topic: Why consolidated statements matter for creditors
prompt: Why are consolidated statements important for creditors? P (equity 1,000, debt 1,000) invests 2,000 in S1 (debt 2,000), which invests 4,000 in S2 (debt 4,000) buying fixed assets of 8,000. Individual debt/equity ratios are 1. What is the consolidated debt/equity ratio?
explanation: Group: assets 8,000; equity = only P's external equity 1,000; financial debt = 1,000 + 2,000 + 4,000 = 7,000 → D/E = 7. The individual statements hide the leverage of the group.

prompt: Parent acquired 40% of company A for 60 (significant influence). A's net income in N+1 is 20. How does the investment appear in the parent's consolidated statements at the end of N+1?

options.text: Investment in associates 68; share of profit of associates 8
Investment 60; dividend income 8
A's assets and liabilities integrated at 40%
Investment at A's market value

explanation: Equity method: cost 60 + 40% × 20 = 68 in one balance-sheet line, and 8 in one income-statement line. No line-by-line integration and no NCI.

topic: Purchase price allocation & consolidated balance sheet
prompt: Prepare the purchase price allocation and the consolidated balance sheet of Palma at the acquisition date.
modelAnswer:
PPA: purchase price 2,600 − book value of Ibiza's equity (400 + 1,000 + 200 = 1,600) = 1,000 difference; valuation difference brand name 600; goodwill = 2,600 − (1,600 + 600) = 400.
Consolidated balance sheet (K€): Land 700; other non-current assets 2,800; brand name 600; goodwill 400; current assets 1,400 → total 5,900. Share capital 800; retained earnings 2,400; net income 200 (equity 3,400 = Palma only); liabilities 2,500 → total 5,900. The investment in Ibiza (2,600) disappears.
keyPoints: Assets: land 700, other NCA 2,800, current 1,400, brand 600, GW 400 = 5,900

steps.title: Book value of the net assets acquired
steps.why: Start the purchase price allocation (PPA) with the subsidiary's equity at the acquisition date – all equity lines count, including the net income of the year.
lines: Ibiza equity = share capital 400 + retained earnings 1,000 + net income 200 = 1,600

steps.title: Identify fair value adjustments
steps.why: IFRS 3: all identifiable assets and liabilities are remeasured at fair value. Ibiza's internally developed brand is not on its own balance sheet (IAS 38 forbids it), but in a business combination it is identifiable and must be recognised.
lines: Brand name: fair value 600 − book value 0 = +600
Other assets: fair value = book value → no adjustment

steps.title: Calculate goodwill
lines: Goodwill = purchase price − fair value of net assets

steps.title: Aggregate and eliminate
steps.why: Full consolidation: add up 100% of the assets and liabilities of both companies, replace the investment in Ibiza by Ibiza's net assets at fair value plus goodwill, and eliminate Ibiza's equity (it is 'bought', so it is not group equity).

steps.title: Check
steps.why: At the acquisition date, group equity equals the parent's equity (800 + 2,400 + 200 = 3,400) – the subsidiary has not yet earned anything for the group.

pitfalls: Using only share capital (400) as Ibiza's book value – retained earnings and net income belong to equity too.
Keeping Ibiza's net income in group equity at the acquisition date.
Forgetting the brand: an internally generated brand is recognised in the PPA.

topic: Purchase price allocation & consolidated balance sheet
prompt: Prepare the consolidated balance sheet of PC at the date of acquisition (with purchase price allocation).
modelAnswer:
PPA: price 3,000 − SA equity 1,200 = 1,800; brand name 600; building +400 → fair value of net assets 2,200; goodwill = 800 (includes the expected synergies, which are not separately identifiable).
Consolidated BS: cash 880; receivables 1,160; inventory 1,350; PP&E 5,870 (4,600 + 870 + 400); brand 600; goodwill 800 → 10,660. Share capital 900; share premium 700; retained earnings 1,210; current liabilities 3,200; long-term debt 4,650 → 10,660.

steps.title: Book value of SA's equity
lines: Share capital 200 + share premium 825 + retained earnings 175 = 1,200

steps.title: Fair value adjustments (IFRS 3)
lines: Brand name (not on SA's balance sheet): +600
Building (part of PP&E): fair value − book value = +400

steps.title: Goodwill
steps.why: Expected synergies (800) cannot be separately identified and measured – they are exactly what goodwill represents. They are NOT added as a separate asset.

steps.title: Consolidated balance sheet at the acquisition date
Check
steps.why: Group equity = PC's equity only (900 + 700 + 1,210 = 2,810). Both sides total 10,660.

pitfalls: Recognising the synergies (800) as a separate intangible AND as goodwill – that counts them twice.
Forgetting to add the +400 fair value step-up to PP&E.

prompt: Explain what non-controlling interest represents and how it is presented in the consolidated balance sheet and income statement.
modelAnswer: Non-controlling interest (NCI) is the share of a subsidiary's equity (net assets) and net income that is not attributable to the parent, i.e. that belongs to minority shareholders. Because the parent controls the subsidiary, 100% of the subsidiary's assets, liabilities, income and expenses are consolidated; NCI is then presented within consolidated equity, separately from equity attributable to the parent, and consolidated net income is split into the group share and the NCI share. A negative NCI means that the subsidiaries concerned have negative equity (accumulated losses).
keyPoints: Share of subsidiary equity not owned by the parent
Net income split into group share and NCI

steps.title: Define NCI
steps.why: Non-controlling interest = the share of a subsidiary's equity (net assets) and of its net income that does not belong to the parent, i.e. that belongs to the minority shareholders. Example: parent owns 80% → NCI 20%.

steps.title: Why NCI appears at all
steps.why: Under control (IFRS 10) the parent fully consolidates: 100% of the subsidiary's assets, liabilities, income and expenses are included, even if it owns less than 100%. The part that is not the parent's has to be shown separately.

steps.title: Presentation in the balance sheet
steps.why: NCI is presented WITHIN consolidated equity, separately from 'equity attributable to owners of the parent' – minority shareholders are owners, not creditors.
lines: NCI = NCI % × subsidiary's equity (at fair value, + share of post-acquisition results)

steps.title: Presentation in the income statement
steps.why: Consolidated net income is calculated with 100% of the subsidiary's result and then split into 'attributable to owners of the parent' and 'attributable to NCI'.
steps.result: NCI: inside equity, separate line; net income split group share / NCI

pitfalls: Consolidating only the parent's percentage of the assets (that is proportionate consolidation, not IFRS 10).

prompt: Prepare PC's consolidated balance sheet as of 31 December N. Give goodwill, consolidated net income and the balance sheet total.
modelAnswer: Goodwill = 160 − 160 = 0. Investment 160 eliminated against SA's capital 100 and pre-acquisition retained earnings 60. Equipment 570, inventory 80, cash 120 → 770. Capital 300, net income 80 + 120 = 200, liabilities 270 → 770.
keyPoints: Investment eliminated against capital 100 + pre-acquisition RE 60
Net income 200 (SA's N result is post-acquisition)

steps.title: Split SA's equity into pre- and post-acquisition
steps.why: Equity existing at the acquisition date was 'bought' and is eliminated against the investment. Everything earned afterwards belongs to the group.

pitfalls: Eliminating SA's net income of N – it was earned after the acquisition.

prompt: Prepare the purchase price allocation and PC's consolidated balance sheet as of 31 December N.
modelAnswer: PPA: 450 − 160 = 290; brand 260; goodwill 30. Consolidated BS 31/12/N: equipment 570, brand 260, goodwill 30, inventory 80, cash 120 → 1,060. Capital 300, net income 200, liabilities 560 → 1,060.

steps.title: Carry the PPA to 31/12/N
steps.why: Brand (indefinite life) and goodwill are not amortised and not impaired → unchanged. SA's N result is post-acquisition.

prompt: Prepare the purchase price allocation and the consolidated balance sheet at the acquisition date.
modelAnswer: Subsidiary equity 100 + 125 + 775 = 1,000; brand +300; PP&E +500 → fair value of net assets 1,800; goodwill 150. Consolidated: cash 655, receivables 988, inventory 1,417, PP&E 5,993, brand 300, goodwill 150 → 9,503. Common stock 818, APIC 607, RE 2,512, current liabilities 1,066, long-term debt 4,500 → 9,503.

steps.title: Book value of the subsidiary's net assets

prompt: Prepare PC's consolidated balance sheet as of 31 December N+1. Give consolidated retained earnings, the group share of net income, NCI and the total.

steps.title: SA's equity at N+1: pre- vs post-acquisition
Consolidated balance sheet 31/12/N+1
steps.why: Full consolidation: 100% of SA's assets and liabilities.

pitfalls: Giving the whole post-acquisition profit to the group – 20% belongs to the NCI.

prompt: Prepare the consolidated income statement for the current year, including the split of net income.
modelAnswer: Sales 9,050,000; COGS 6,575,000; gross profit 2,475,000; operating expenses 1,930,000; consolidated net income 545,000, of which NCI 30% × 295,000 = 88,500 and owners of the parent 456,500.
keyPoints: 100% of SA's income and expenses added

results.label: Attributable to owners of the parent

steps.title: Add 100% of each line
steps.why: Full consolidation integrates all income and expenses of SA, even though PC owns 70%.

pitfalls: Adding only 70% of SA's sales and expenses.

prompt: Prepare PC's consolidated balance sheet as of 31 December N+1 using the equity method. Give the investment in AC, consolidated net income and the total. What would change if PC had paid 45 instead of 40?
modelAnswer: AC equity N+1 = 430; increase since acquisition 270 → PC's share 25% = 67.5. Investment in AC = 40 + 67.5 = 107.5. Consolidated RE = 60 + 25% × 120 = 90; NI = 100 + 25% × 150 = 137.5. Total 480 + 107.5 + 230 = 817.5 = 300 + 90 + 137.5 + 290. If paid 45: goodwill 5 included in the investment (not shown separately) → investment 112.5.
keyPoints: NI 137.5 incl. share of AC's profit 37.5

steps.title: Equity method principle (IAS 28)
steps.why: Associates are NOT consolidated line by line. The investment is carried at cost and increased/decreased by the investor's share of the associate's post-acquisition results (dividends reduce it).

steps.title: AC's post-acquisition equity
lines: Increase: 270 (RE +120 from year N, NI N+1 150)

steps.title: Price 45 instead of 40
lines: Goodwill stays inside the investment line (not shown separately) → investment 112.5

pitfalls: Adding AC's assets line by line (that is full consolidation).
Showing the goodwill of an associate as a separate asset.

statement: Consolidated financial statements represent the financial situation of economic entities.
explanation: True. Consolidated statements present the group – several legal entities under common control – as ONE economic entity.

statement: A parent company is a company that controls another company by owning at least 20% of the voting rights of the controlled entity.
explanation: Wrong. 20% is the presumption for SIGNIFICANT INFLUENCE (associate). Control is presumed above 50% of the voting rights – and what counts is control itself (power, exposure to variable returns, link between them), not a percentage.

statement: Companies under significant influence of the parent company are part of the scope of consolidation.
explanation: True in the broad sense: the scope of consolidation covers all entities the group accounts for with a consolidation method – subsidiaries (full consolidation) AND associates (equity method). Careful: associates are NOT fully consolidated. (The mock questions also contain the opposite version – read 'scope' as 'accounted for by a consolidation method'.)

statement: A parent company holding more than 50% of another company usually reflects a relationship of significant influence.
explanation: Wrong. More than 50% of the voting rights usually means CONTROL → subsidiary, full consolidation. Significant influence is presumed between 20% and 50%. Hinweis: Der Lösungsschlüssel der Mock-Fragen markiert hier 'True' – nach IFRS 10 / IAS 28 ist das falsch.

statement: Non-controlling interest is essentially the portion of equity (net assets) in a subsidiary that is not attributable to the parent company.
explanation: True – this is the IFRS 10 definition: equity in a subsidiary not attributable, directly or indirectly, to the parent. It is presented within consolidated equity, separately from the parent's share. Hinweis: Der Lösungsschlüssel der Mock-Fragen markiert hier 'False' – die Aussage entspricht aber wörtlich der Definition.

prompt: Non-controlling interest in the consolidated balance sheet represents …

options.text: investments (financial assets) in companies that the parent company does not control
equity provided by shareholders (other than the parent's shareholders) to subsidiaries that the parent does not own 100%
debt provided to subsidiaries that the parent company does not own 100%
investments in companies on which the parent company has significant influence

explanation: NCI = the minority shareholders' share in the equity of subsidiaries that are not wholly owned. It is equity (not debt) and has nothing to do with financial assets or associates (those appear as investments on the asset side).

prompt: Company A buys 100% of the shares of Company B for 800. The book value of B is 500. At the acquisition date B had internally developed a brand name with a fair value of 100. Which statement about the consolidated financial statements is correct?

options.text: The goodwill of this acquisition is 300
When accounting for Company B the full consolidation method has to be applied
Since the brand name is internally generated it cannot be accounted for
If the brand name is accounted for, IFRS require it to be amortised over its useful life

explanation: 100% → control → full consolidation. In the purchase price allocation the brand IS recognised (internally generated for B, but acquired for the group): goodwill = 800 − (500 + 100) = 200, not 300. A brand usually has an indefinite useful life → no amortisation, annual impairment test.

prompt: IOWA bought 100% of VIP Ltd on 31 December N1; goodwill of 800,000 was recognised in IOWA's consolidated statements. What do you recommend for goodwill in the N2 consolidated statements?

options.text: Goodwill has to be amortised over a free term, depending on IOWA's estimates
Goodwill is not amortised, but an impairment test has to be performed every year
The value of goodwill was estimated at the acquisition date and will never change
Goodwill is re-estimated every year: written down if the new estimate is below 800,000 and increased if it is above

explanation: IFRS 3 / IAS 36: goodwill is not amortised but tested for impairment at least annually. It can be written down, but never written up (an impairment of goodwill is never reversed).

prompt: Non-controlling interests (NCI) in a consolidated balance sheet have strongly increased in N compared with the previous year. Which explanation is CORRECT? NCI increased because …

options.text: the parent invested in another company, acquiring 20% and hence significant influence
for one subsidiary the parent sold part of its shares, decreasing its ownership from 80% to 60%
the parent company increased its share capital in N
the parent invested in another company, acquiring 100% and hence control

explanation: Selling shares while keeping control raises the minorities' share from 20% to 40% → NCI increase. An associate (20%) does not create NCI; a parent's capital increase raises the group share of equity; a 100% acquisition creates no NCI.

prompt: When a subsidiary is acquired some time after the first day of the fiscal year, which statement is true?

options.text: Income from the subsidiary is not recognised until there is an entire year of consolidated operations
Income from the subsidiary is recognised from the date of acquisition to year-end
The excess of cost over the acquired net assets is recognised at the beginning of the fiscal year
Income from the subsidiary is recognised for the entire year

explanation: A subsidiary is consolidated from the date control is obtained: only income and expenses earned after the acquisition date enter the consolidated income statement. Profits before that date are part of the acquired equity.

prompt: When a company holds 50% of the capital (ordinary shares) of another company, it exercises …

options.text: exclusive control in all cases
joint control in all cases
exclusive control in some cases

explanation: 50% is not a majority. Control depends on the facts: e.g. a shareholders' agreement, the right to appoint the majority of the board or double voting rights can give exclusive control; otherwise it may be joint control or significant influence.

prompt: On 31 December year 1, PC acquired 100% of SA's shares for $450. SA's equity is $160 on its balance sheet. SA has developed a brand name whose fair value is estimated at $250 at the acquisition date. What goodwill is recognised in the consolidated balance sheet?
explanation: Fair value of SA's identifiable net assets = 160 + brand 250 = 410. Goodwill = 450 − 410 = 40. (290 forgets the brand.)

prompt: PC acquired 100% of SA for $150 on 31 December N−1, when SA's equity was $150 (capital 100, net income 50). On 31 December N, SA's equity shows capital 100, retained earnings 50 and net income 130. PC reports a net income of $80. What is the consolidated net income for year N?
explanation: Consolidated net income = PC 80 + 100% of SA's post-acquisition result 130 = 210. SA's retained earnings of 50 were earned BEFORE the acquisition – they are part of the acquired equity and eliminated against the investment. Hinweis: Der Lösungsschlüssel der Mock-Fragen markiert hier $260 – das zählt die vor dem Erwerb erzielten 50 mit und ist nicht nachvollziehbar.

prompt: Goodwill corresponds to …

options.text: the difference between the acquisition price of the shares and the share held in the subsidiary's equity
the difference between the purchase price of the shares and the share held in the subsidiary's equity revalued at fair value at the date of acquisition
the difference between the purchase price of the shares and the share held in the subsidiary's equity remeasured at fair value at the date of consolidation

explanation: Goodwill = purchase price − share in the FAIR VALUE of the identifiable net assets, measured at the ACQUISITION date (purchase price allocation). Book values (a) or later remeasurements (c) are wrong.

prompt: PC acquired 70% of SA for $210 on 31 December N. SA's equity is $300 (capital 140, net income 160) and its liabilities are $60. What non-controlling interest is reported in the consolidated balance sheet on that date?
explanation: NCI = 30% × SA's equity 300 = 90 (liabilities are not part of equity). Goodwill = 210 − 70% × 300 = 0.
